keySentence: Shared laws transform individuals into a true community — without them there is only chaos.

facts.Page story text 1 (draft, teacher check: The Bandar-log were the monkey people of the jungle. They had no Law and no leader and no promises to anyone. They grabbed at anything they wanted and forgot it quickly. Other animals avoided them because they could not be trusted. The wolf pack and the elephants were different from them. Rules are not chains — they hold a community together inside. Shared laws transform individuals into a true community — without them there is only chaos.
facts.Page story text 2 (draft, teacher check: The Bandar-log were the monkey people who lived above the rest of the jungle in the treetops. They had no Law and no leader and no memory of any promise they had ever made to anyone. They grabbed at whatever they wanted and forgot it the moment something new caught their eye. The other jungle animals avoided them not because they were dangerous but because they were unreliable. You could not trust a Bandar-log because they had no standard they consistently held themselves to. The Law was what separated the wolf pack and the elephant herds from that kind of scattered chaos. Rules are not chains — they are the invisible architecture that holds a community together from inside. Shared laws transform individuals into a true community — without them there is only chaos.
facts.Page story text 3 (draft, teacher check: The Bandar-log, the monkey people of the Indian jungle, lived noisily and restlessly in the high branches above the rest of the forest. They had no Law and no leader and no memory of any promise they had ever made to any living creature. Whatever they wanted in any given moment, they grabbed at — and then forgot about the moment something new caught their wandering attention. The other animals of the jungle avoided them carefully, not because they were strong or dangerous but because they could not be relied upon for anything at all. You could not negotiate with a Bandar-log, you could not depend on a Bandar-log, you could not build anything at all with a Bandar-log as a partner. What separated the wolf pack and the elephant herds and the other genuine communities of the jungle from the Bandar-log was exactly one thing — the Law. Rules, Mowgli came to understand, were not chains designed to restrict the strong — they were the invisible architecture that made genuine community possible at all. Without them, you got the Bandar-log: a crowd of individuals pretending to be a group, going nowhere together and accomplishing nothing that lasted longer than an afternoon. Shared laws transform individuals into a true community — without them there is only chaos.
